description: Headless Python script that gives BIDS names to the series HeuDiConv marked __dup-NN. It reads each sidecar: a bold series described as _SBRef becomes sbref, magnitude and phase of one acquisition get part-mag and part-phase, and repeats of one protocol get run numbers in SeriesNumber order. scans.tsv and IntendedFor follow the new names, and sourcedata is renamed to match. The tidy dataset is written as a new folder whose unchanged files are hard links to the input.

bids_dir.description: BIDS dataset from HeuDiConv, possibly with __dup-NN series.
The dataset with the duplicate series renamed; HeuDiConv's .heudiconv state is left out.

summary.description: renamed [{from, to, why}], unresolved groups, and remainingDup: series still carrying a __dup marker.

block.label: Tidy BIDS Names
block.description: Rename HeuDiConv __dup series from their sidecars.

requirements: Python 3.10+ (standard library only); set NEUROFLOW_PYTHON to choose the interpreter
neuroflow/launch.description: python_tool.mjs finds a Python interpreter, then calls nf_bids_tidy.run(bids_dir), which writes the tidy dataset to $NEUROFLOW_OUTPUT_DIR/bids and appends a provenance line listing the renames.

useWhen: A HeuDiConv dataset has __dup-NN series, typically magnitude/phase reconstructions, SBRef images or repeated protocols.
Run it between heudiconv-reproin and any tool that expects valid BIDS names.

avoidWhen.when: A person should decide the names: review the session interactively instead.

preconditions: bids_dir has JSON sidecars with SeriesNumber, SeriesDescription and ImageType (dcm2niix writes them).
effects: Writes a new dataset to <output dir>/bids; the input is not changed. Unchanged files are hard links, so the copy costs little disk on one filesystem.
Series still sharing a name after the rules keep HeuDiConv's names; the step log and provenance list them.

duration.basis: One 4.5 GB session with 32 series, hard-linked on one APFS volume.

failures.meaning: No Python environment was found for the tool.
failures.remedy: Set NEUROFLOW_PYTHON to a Python 3.10+ interpreter.
